items.title: Unfiltered credentialIds passed to cache status query
items.body: connectedCalendars.handler.ts builds credentialIds by mapping every connectedCalendar without filtering null/undefined values or non-Google credentials and calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds() unconditionally, even when the list is empty. Null credentialIds will fail Prisma validation for an Int filter, and the query runs for Outlook and other integrations that never have CalendarCache rows. Filter to defined Google credentialIds and skip the query when empty.

items.title: Resolve the env file path independently of the caller's working directory
items.body: `ENV_FILE` is relative to the current working directory, not this script's location. Running the script from the repository root (for example, `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) reads or creates `../.env` instead of the repository's `.env`, so the app does not receive the configured webhook URL. Resolve the path from the script directory or set it explicitly.

items.title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared tsx
items.body: dev:cron was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency of @calcom/web) to npx tsx, but tsx is not listed in this package. yarn dev:cron will download an arbitrary tsx via npx or fail offline/in CI, instead of using the previously pinned local runner.

items.title: Failed Init leaks server context
items.body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context for the server, stores cancel in the server struct, then calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously. On Init error it returns nil, err without calling cancel, leaking the context and any resources started before the failure. Call cancel before returning the error.

items.title: BuildIndex span context is still discarded
items.body: The PR's stated trace fix is to pass the span context into child work (`ctx, span := tracer.Start`). BuildIndex, which this change edits, still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(...)`. The builder callback and SQL list work started from the incoming ctx are not children of the BuildIndex span, so the index-build trace stays disconnected from the work it wraps.

items.title: Mode 3 tests never assert that the asynchronous legacy write actually happens, and would pass even if it never runs
items.body: All Mode 3 unit tests (TestMode3_Create, TestMode3_Delete, TestMode3_Update, TestMode3_DeleteCollection) exercise the dual writer and assert only on the unified-storage result. Because the legacy write now runs in a detached goroutine, the tests return before (or regardless of whether) d.Legacy.* is invoked; the mocks' legacy expectations are set up but never asserted with m.AssertCalled / AssertExpectations, and there is no synchronization (e.g. waiting on a channel or Eventually) to observe the async call. Consequently the tests cannot detect the critical regression where the legacy write never executes (e.g. due to the request-context cancellation bug in dualwriter_mode3.go): they would still pass. Each test that sets up setupLegacyFn should wait for and assert the legacy call (e.g. assert.Eventually on a mock call count, or a WaitGroup/channel in the mock), and there should be a test asserting that a legacy failure does not affect the returned result (the intended mode-3 semantics).

items.title: Tests don't verify async legacy writes
items.body: The tests never wait for or assert that the legacy mock is called after the unified write. The legacy mocks are set up but unverified, and the goroutines may outlive the test or race with mock state. The error case sets up a Legacy Create expectation that is never used.

items.title: getLoginPredicate dereferences possibly-null IDP config
items.body: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() now evaluates idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC). If an IdentityProviderModel has a null config map the call throws NullPointerException. The predicate is invoked on every create/remove/update invalidation path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate), so a single IDP with null config breaks IDP writes with a 500 instead of correctly deciding to (not) invalidate the login caches.

items.title: Login-cache invalidation uses org-wrapped isEnabled and can skip
items.body: update() loads the pre-image with getById(), which returns the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false when the IdP is linked to a missing or disabled organization (or when the organization provider is disabled), even if the stored enabled flag is true. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate treats that wrapper as "not a login IdP". If the update also makes the raw model ineligible (enabled=false, hideOnLogin, link-only, or broker-public cleared), both predicate checks fail and the method returns without invalidating the getForLogin list keys. Those lists were built from the JPA enabled/hide/link/public filters, so they still contain the IdP. After the org is enabled again, getForLogin keeps returning it, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin/linkOnly/broker-public, so a hidden or link-only broker can show up on the login page until some other event drops the cache. Compare against the delegate/raw model (or always invalidate login keys on update).

items.title: Match statistics recorded inside the user save transaction are rolled back on failure
items.body: Because `should_block?` saves the BlockedEmail record during the User's validation, the write happens inside the User save transaction. In `save!`/`create_for_email`, a blocked email raises RecordInvalid and the transaction rolls back, losing the match_count/last_match_at update. Statistics are then inconsistent depending on the call path (`save` vs `save!`).

items.title: ANY() with empty array produces SQL that may behave unexpectedly
items.body: In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, `teamIds` always contains at least `options.orgId`, so `ANY(${teamIds})` is never empty. However, in buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (line 201), `userIdsFromTeam` could theoretically be empty if the team has no members, but the code guards with `if (userIdsFromTeam.length > 0)`. In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition line 168, `uniqueUserIds` is guarded by `if (userIdsFromOrg.length > 0)`. So empty arrays are guarded. However, the `ANY()` operator with a JavaScript array in Prisma.sql requires the array to be non-empty; if somehow an empty array reaches `ANY(${{}})`, PostgreSQL would throw a syntax error or return unexpected results. The guards are present, but this is fragile — if the guard logic changes, empty arrays would cause runtime SQL errors. Consider adding an explicit assertion or using a different pattern for empty arrays.

items.title: Public functions removed/renamed without updating other callers or tests
items.body: The PR deletes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `SimpleCheckIn` and the failure-status maps from `mark_failed.py`, and renames two of them. The diff shows no updates to tests or other modules that import them from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`. Any such import will now raise ImportError. Existing tests that patch `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.*` (e.g. `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` or `create_issue_platform_occurrence`) will also break. Update the callers and tests, or re-export the old names.

cal.com__22345.text: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

cal.com__22532.text: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

discourse-graphite__3.text: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

grafana__90045.text: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.

grafana__97529.text: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

keycloak__32918.text: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

sentry__80528.text: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.
